content: 1. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with P-gp inhibitors is necessary, reduce the daily dose of afatinib by 10 mg if not tolerated. 2. Both albuterol and erythromycin lactobionate increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of alfentanil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Erythromycin lactobionate and alfuzosin both increase the QTc interval. Erythromycin lactobionate also increases the level or effect of alfuzosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of aliskiren by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 6. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of alosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of alvimopan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of ambrisentan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 12. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of amifampridine through other mechanisms. Amifampridine can cause seizures, and coadministration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may increase this risk. Monitor closely. 13. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both amiodarone and erythromycin lactobionate increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Amisulpride and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended if coadministered. 16. Amitriptyline and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Amobarbital decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing elimination. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 19. Amoxapine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of amoxicillin and ampicillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 21. Anagrelide and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Anastrozole increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 23. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III by decreasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. 25. Apomorphine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Aprepitant increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of aprepitant by the same mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Arformoterol and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of argatroban by decreasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Aripiprazole and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of armodafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Armodafinil decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 31. Arsenic trioxide and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Artemether and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Erythromycin lactobionate and artemether/lumefantrine both increase the QTc interval. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Asenapine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Atazanavir increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of atazanavir by the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of atogepant through other mechanisms. Adjust the dose of atogepant to 10 mg or 30 mg daily when coadministered with OATP inhibitors. Monitor closely. 37. Atomoxetine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This increases the risk of myopathy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Reduce the maximum dose of avanafil to 50 mg, not exceeding once every 24 hours, for patients taking moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of avapritinib and monitor closely. 41. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor closely and reduce the dose if necessary. 42. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the level or effect of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It also decreases their level or effect by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine live through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 46. Erythromycin lactobionate and bedaquiline both increase the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended, and therapy should be modified as needed. 47. Belzutifan decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate according to its prescribing information. 48. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of bemiparin by decreasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of bendamustine by decreasing its conversion to active metabolites. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Berotralstat also increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce the dose of betrixaban to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. Monitor closely. 52. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the level or effect of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of bivalirudin by decreasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 55. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while bosentan decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor. Monitor closely. 59. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of bromocriptine through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
